title: Pixelasset coat palette (base colour → coat colour)
description: A coat of an ingested third-party family: a colour-for-colour correspondence measured off one named sheet, applied to another coat's geometry. Deliberately NOT palette.schema.json's `coats`, which is a seven-role style ramp (OUTLINE…ACCENT) replacing `roles` wholesale for Path C's role-character templates. These colours have no roles and cannot acquire them — #5e3420 is not SHADOW in any style sense, it is whatever the pack's artist used. Folding them in would also mean re-measuring a third-party PNG bumps palette_v1, versioning the pack inside the §19 style record and changing every Path C asset's palette_version. §23 is satisfied instead by every coat of a family sharing one key space, named in `base` and checked for set equality.

base.description: The coat whose colours are this coat's keys. Every coat of a family declares the same base, and `map`'s key set is checked against it — that shared key space is the thing variants actually share.

source.description: The one sheet this coat was measured from. Pinned to a single sheet on purpose: the pack is not self-consistent across its own sheet families, so a coat that matched all of them cannot exist. Verified at extraction and in the tests, never during a build — see coat.verify_source.

map.description: One row per colour of the base coat's visible palette, ordered by pixel count descending so two coat files diff row for row. A list of rows rather than a YAML mapping because yaml.safe_load silently keeps the last of duplicate keys, which is the exact failure that must be caught; and rather than two parallel lists because those encode the correspondence in line numbers, so a reorder would silently remap the whole coat. Key distinctness is enforced by the loader, not here: JSON Schema 2020-12 has no unique-by-property keyword, and uniqueItems only dedupes whole rows. A row is addressed by `from` (a colour) or by `role` (a name the base coat gives that colour) — the loader resolves `role` to `from`, so authoring by intent and diffing by colour are the same file format.

from.description: A colour of the base coat. These are the keys and must be pairwise distinct. The base coat declares every row with both `from` and `role`; a derived coat gives one or the other.

to.description: What that colour becomes. Duplicates are legal and intentional: a coat whose art uses fewer colours than the base names the same target twice, which is how black's eleven colours cover bay's thirteen steps.

role.description: What the colour IS, so a coat can be authored by intent rather than by hex. Declared once, in the base coat, and derived from the artwork rather than assumed — see coat_bay.yaml for the measurement behind each name. A derived coat may address a row by `role` instead of `from`; the loader resolves it.

roles.description: Role groups, declared by the base coat only. A group is a set of roles that belong to one feature of the artwork, so an intent like "lighten the mane" addresses a group rather than three hex values. Derived from the art: the marking test in coat_bay.yaml is what separates `mane` from `body`.

accept_collapse.description: Role pairs this coat deliberately renders indistinguishable, each with the reason. A collapse is not automatically a defect — a black horse's mane really is not lighter than its body, and a chestnut's mane really is close to its coat — but it costs the hatched strand texture, so it is signed off rather than ignored. §27: validation reports and an intended finding is accepted WITH the reason attached, never silently dropped. Keys are 'ROLE_A/ROLE_B' with the roles in alphabetical order.
